witnesses.separates: Three 4 cells at three corners of a 1x2 box: $RectMarker reads them as a marker and draws a copy past its empty corner (11, 9); the concept, which reads only 2-apart square boxes, leaves them as they are.

Every marker spans a box whose corners are 3 apart: $DerivedStride derives stride 3 and draws a copy at the marker whose empty corner is (12, 5); the concept, at stride 2, finds no marker and so no template marker, and is undefined.

A 1x7 template whose centroid (3, 7) lies nearer the empty corner (5, 7) of another marker than its own marker's (3, 4): $NearestCentroid takes (5, 7) as the template's marker, so its copies land on rows 5 and 11; the concept's copies land on rows 5 and 9.

A template that is not symmetric about the diagonal through its marker's empty corner, and a marker whose empty corner (6, 10) is the top-right one: the concept mirrors the template across rows, and $Rotate turns it a quarter turn.
The template is drawn in 3: $AnyColorTemplate copies it in 3 at (11, 10); the concept, reading color 2, finds no template and is undefined.
The template holds 2 and 3 cells: $AnyColorTemplate copies both colors, and the concept copies only the 2 cells.
The markers are drawn in 3: $DerivedMarkerColor derives marker color 3 and draws a copy at (11, 10); the concept, reading color 4, finds no marker and is undefined.

The copies at (7, 5) and (5, 7) each cover a cell of the other's marker, (7, 7) and (5, 5), at a background cell of the template: the concept keeps those 4 cells, and $BoxStamp writes background over them.

The copy at the marker whose empty corner is (1, 11) runs one row past the top edge, and the corners (1, 3) and (1, 9) lie 6 apart: the concept draws the rows inside the grid; RectMarker, which from side 6 puts (1, 9) in two rectangle triples, is undefined.
`background=DominantColor` from the stored value: train 0 with 0 and 1 swapped

A three-cell template in the L of a stride-2 marker, the rarest color: the derived marker color with the rarest color as background reads 4 alone and copies; with the stored background both 2 and 4 split into triples and it is undefined.
`template_color=RarestColor` from the stored value: train 0 with 2 and 1 swapped

Every marker spans a box whose corners are 3 apart, and the 16-cell sides admit 3 tiles: the stride derived from the tile counts includes 3 and draws the copy at the marker whose empty corner is (12, 5); the stored stride 2 finds no marker and is undefined.

Markers whose corners are 3 apart, with blank columns 4, 5, 10 and 11 cutting the columns into 3 tiles: the stride derived from the separator lattice includes 3 and draws the copy at the marker whose empty corner is (11, 12); the stored stride 2 finds no marker and is undefined.

The two markers' corners (1, 1) and (9, 1) lie 8 apart, so at side 8 the corner (1, 1) is in two rectangle triples: RectMarker with the stored sides 2 to 8 is undefined, and with the sides derived from the 14-cell tile counts, which leave out 8, it draws the concept's copy.

The two markers' corners (1, 1) and (9, 1) lie 8 apart, so at side 8 the corner (1, 1) is in two rectangle triples: RectMarker with the stored sides 2 to 8 is undefined, and with the sides derived from the separator lattice, which leave out 8, it draws the concept's copy.

A 2x7 template with a 3 at its marker's empty corner (3, 3), a hole row over its own cell (4, 3), and a centroid nearer the empty corner (5, 6) of a marker at a quarter turn: the source, the transform, the stamp and the template color each change the output, and every case is defined.

The long-template layout with markers whose corners are 3 apart: the extents that read stride 3 draw the copies, with the source, transform, stamp and template color each changing them; the stored stride, the rectangle reading and the stride-2 marker color reading are undefined.

The long-template layout with the quarter-turn marker squashed into a 1x2 box: RectMarker copies at it and the stored stride does not; DerivedStride and the stride-2 derived marker color, whose marker cells do not split, are undefined.

The long-template layout with a third marker whose column-1 corners lie 8 from the source marker's: at side 8 its corners are in two rectangle triples, so RectMarker with the stored sides is undefined and with sides derived from the 20-cell grid, which leave out 8, draws the copies.

The long-template layout with markers in 5: the derived marker color copies, with the source, transform, stamp and template color each changing the copies; the stored marker color finds no marker and is undefined.

The long-template layout on a background of 1: the dominant-color background keeps the template to its own cells and writes 1 into a box copy's holes; the stored background reads the 1 cells as template and writes 0.

The long-template layout with three 5 cells in the L of a stride-2 marker, the rarest color: the derived marker color with the rarest color as background reads 4 alone and copies; with the stored background both 4 and 5 split into triples and it is undefined.

The long-template layout with a one-color template of eight cells, fewer than the marker cells, so the rarest color is the template's: the source, the transform and the stamp each change the copies of the rarest-color template too.

A background of 1 with three 0 cells in the L of a stride-2 marker and a two-cell template: the derived marker color with the stored background leaves 0 out and copies; with the dominant color as background, 0 and 4 both split into triples and it is undefined.

The copy-past-edge input with a third marker, so the template's color is the rarest: the corners (1, 9) and (1, 3) lie 6 apart and make a second rectangle triple from side 6, so RectMarker with the sides from the tile counts, which hold 7, is undefined, and with the sides from the separator lattice it copies.
The long-template layout with markers whose corners are 5 apart on a 16-cell grid: DerivedStride reads stride 5 and copies; the stride from the tile counts of 16 holds no 5 and is undefined.
The stride-five-long input with the marker stride assigned 5: the stored stride copies; the stride from the tile counts of 16 holds no 5 and is undefined.

The long-template layout with content on rows and columns 6, 8, 9 and 10, so no separator lattice fits: RectMarker with the sides from the tile counts copies, and with the sides from the separator lattice, which are none, it is undefined.

The long-template layout with markers whose corners are 6 apart, and the marker's longest side assigned 6: RectMarker with the stored side copies; with the sides from the tile counts of 20, which hold no 6, or from the separator lattice it is undefined.

A stride-2 source marker nested in a stride-3 L that shares its empty corner (4, 4): the stored stride and the stride from the separator lattice, which holds 2 alone, copy; the stride from the tile counts also reads the stride-3 L as the template's marker, whose reading has no target, and the two readings give two colors at the copy cells.

The long-template layout with markers in 0 on a background of 1: the derived marker color with the dominant color as background reads the 0 markers and copies; with the stored background 0 it finds no marker color and is undefined.

A 10x20 grid whose template rows outnumber the 0 cells: with the stored background the template is its 2 and 3 cells and a box copy writes 0; with the dominant color 2 as background the template is the 0 and 3 cells, which no marker's corner bounds, and a box copy writes 2.

The marker_stride=SepTileCount input with one template cell removed, so the template's color is the rarest: the stride from the separator lattice copies the rarest-color template; the stored stride finds no marker and is undefined.

Two clusters of nine 4 cells, each splitting both into stride-2 and into stride-3 triples, with a two-cell template from a stride-2 empty corner (3, 3) to a stride-3 empty corner (5, 5): the stride from the separator lattice, 2 alone, copies; the stride from the tile counts reads both strides, each with a template marker, and the two readings give two colors at the copy cells.

Two clusters of nine 4 cells, each splitting both into stride-2 and into stride-3 triples, and a one-cell template at (3, 6), the empty corner of a stride-2 marker and of a stride-3 marker: the stride from the separator lattice, 2 alone, copies the cell; the stride from the tile counts reads both strides and gives two colors at the copy cells.

A 16x16 grid whose most frequent color 1 lies in stride-2 L triples among cells of six other colors, with blank-0 rows 7 and 8, three 4 markers and a two-cell template of the rarest color 2: the derived marker color with the dominant 1 as background reads 4 alone and copies; with the rarest color as background both 1 and 4 split into triples and it is undefined.
